data.narrative:
Standard Bots, a Series B robotics and manufacturing company, is valued against a peer set spanning one public comparable (277810.KQ) and eight private companies in the same sector, with particular focus on four direct-stage peers: Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B Series B), Dexterity ($1.6B Series B), Hadrian ($1.6B Series C), and Nimble Robotics ($1.0B Series C).

Two triangulation methods anchor the analysis. Stage-progression applies a 1.9x multiplier to Standard Bots' $200M total raised as a valuation proxy, yielding $380M. Peer-median analysis across the four same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables produces a $1.6B implied valuation, with the peer set ranging from $1.0B to $1.8B. These approaches diverge materially, reflecting the substantial variance in how Series B robotics companies are capitalized within the current market.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $323M on the low end to $1.9B on the high end, with a median of $1.0B. The wide dispersion—driven by methodological divergence rather than peer consensus—reflects real uncertainty in how to anchor a Series B company without disclosed revenue or path-to-profitability metrics. Stage-progression anchors conservatively; peer comparables suggest the market has priced robotics assets at substantially higher multiples. Capital structure, differentiation in core technology, and pipeline quality remain critical to narrowing this band.
